newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Meralco sees low returns on workers demands.
newsitem.headline: Meralco sees low returns on workers demands.

text.p: The Manila Electric Co, the country's biggest power distributor, said it will ask the Supreme Court to review a new collective bargaining agreement (CBA) with its employees that may lead to lower returns for the company and an increase in power rates.

"The entire CBA will amount to two billion pesos (over two years) and this will mean that our return-on-rate base will go down and may even reach below the mandated eight percent," Meralco spokesperson Elpi Cuna said.
Cuna said Meralco may not be able to fulfill its target of not raising its distribution charges until the year 2000 if the CBA is pushed through.

The Department of Labour and Employment (DOLE) approved a CBA for the Meralco Employees Workers Association (Mewa) that will mean a 4,400 peso monthly pay hike spread over a two year period for each the union's 4,000 members. The Meralco management and Mewa earlier sought the DOLE's intervention when a deadlock was reached on the CBA.
"We hope to submit our petition to the Supreme Court by Thursday or Friday. If the CBA pushes through, its going to be a bad signal for the entire business community," said Cuna.
Mewa president Numeriano Villalobos said that the union will file notice of a strike within the week citing unfair labour practices if the company appeals against the CBA.
He said that the CBA will only amount to extra wage bills of 775 million pesos over two years and not two billion pesos.
